backlog.summary: First backlog draft for the online building permit portal of the Municipality of Seeberg (fictional). Today applications arrive on paper in three printed copies, roughly six out of ten are incomplete, and the permit clerk receives about ten status calls a day. The council wants a first version live by next summer that covers online submission and status tracking. Integration with the canton can follow later. Key constraints are data storage in Switzerland, logging of every dossier access for legal proceedings, German and English language versions, compliance with the federal accessibility standard, retention for the life of the building, and electronic delivery of rulings only with the applicant's consent. One open conflict needs a council decision: whether paper submissions remain possible (Daniel Rossi) or the process becomes digital-only with counter scanning (Monika Keller).

personas.name: Architect / builder (professional applicant)
personas.description: Submits about 80% of applications on behalf of owners. Already produces plans as PDF, sometimes up to 200 MB, and will fall back to paper if uploading is slow.

personas.name: Private homeowner (applicant)
personas.description: Submits small projects such as garden sheds or solar panels. Often older and not comfortable with computers. Wants to know the status of the application.

personas.name: Permit clerk
personas.description: Checks applications for completeness, requests missing documents, answers status calls and coordinates reviews with other offices (Daniel Rossi).

personas.name: Head of Building Department
personas.description: Owns the digitalisation goal, decides on process questions together with the council and controls what applicants may see (Monika Keller).

personas.name: Fire protection reviewer
personas.description: External reviewer from the regional authority, not the municipality. Reviews plans and gives a statement, currently taking three weeks on average.

personas.name: Counter staff
personas.description: Municipal staff at the counter who may digitise paper applications from applicants such as older homeowners, if paper submission remains allowed.

personas.name: IT coordinator
personas.description: Responsible for infrastructure, data protection, access control and audit logging (Sandra Frei).

epics.title: Online application submission
epics.goal: Applicants can submit a complete building permit application with all documents online instead of on paper.

epics.title: Completeness checking
epics.goal: Reduce incomplete applications and the clerk's time spent writing completeness letters, with the target of cutting them in half.

epics.title: Status tracking
epics.goal: Applicants can see the status of their application online, which reduces status phone calls, without exposing internal comments.

epics.title: Review by other offices
epics.goal: Internal and external offices such as fire protection review plans and submit statements directly in the system instead of by internal mail.

epics.title: Decision and electronic delivery
epics.goal: Formal rulings can be delivered electronically to applicants who consent to electronic delivery.

epics.title: Access control, audit and paper channel
epics.goal: Secure role-based access, a complete audit trail for appeals, and a defined approach for paper submissions.

stories.title: Submit application online
stories.i_want: to fill in the building permit application form and submit it online
stories.so_that: I no longer have to send the application and plans in three printed copies
stories.statement: As an architect, I want to fill in the building permit application form and submit it online, so that I no longer have to send the application and plans in three printed copies.

acceptance_criteria.given: an architect has completed all mandatory fields of the application form and attached all required documents
acceptance_criteria.then: the application is stored with a unique reference number and the status "received"

acceptance_criteria.given: an application has been submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: the applicant sees a confirmation showing the reference number and the submission date and time

acceptance_criteria.given: a mandatory form field is empty
acceptance_criteria.then: submission is blocked and the empty field is identified by name

stories.priority_rationale: The council explicitly requires online submission in the first version due next summer.
source_quotes: Our goal is that applications can be submitted fully online.
but submission online and status tracking should be there.
stories.notes: Foundation for US-2 to US-5. Depends on the applicant login approach (see open question on authentication).

stories.title: Upload large PDF plans
stories.i_want: to upload plan documents as PDF files of up to 200 MB each
stories.so_that: I can submit the plans I already produce without splitting or printing them
stories.statement: As an architect, I want to upload plan documents as PDF files of up to 200 MB each, so that I can submit the plans I already produce without splitting or printing them.

acceptance_criteria.given: an architect has a 200 MB PDF plan
acceptance_criteria.when: they upload it to an application
acceptance_criteria.then: the upload completes and the file is listed in the application with its name and size

acceptance_criteria.given: an architect selects a file that is not a PDF for a plan document
acceptance_criteria.then: the upload is rejected with a message stating that plans must be PDF files

acceptance_criteria.given: an upload is in progress
acceptance_criteria.then: a progress indicator shows the percentage uploaded

acceptance_criteria.given: an upload is interrupted
acceptance_criteria.then: the architect is informed that the upload failed and can restart it without losing the other documents already uploaded

stories.priority_rationale: Without large-file upload, online submission does not work, and Daniel warned that architects will keep sending paper if uploads are slow.
source_quotes: Plans come as PDF from the architects anyway.
Some files are huge, 200 megabytes is not unusual.
If uploading plans takes forever, architects will just keep sending paper.
stories.notes: The maximum file size and the upload time target are open questions. Storage must respect NFR-1 (data in Switzerland).

stories.title: See missing documents before submission
stories.i_want: to see a checklist of the required documents and which of them are still missing before I submit
stories.so_that: I can complete the application without receiving a completeness letter
stories.statement: As an architect, I want to see a checklist of the required documents and which of them are still missing before I submit, so that I can complete the application without receiving a completeness letter.

acceptance_criteria.given: an application is in draft
acceptance_criteria.when: the architect opens the document section
acceptance_criteria.then: a checklist shows the application form, site plan, floor plans, sections and elevations, each marked as provided or missing

acceptance_criteria.given: a required document is missing
acceptance_criteria.then: submission is blocked and every missing document is listed by name

acceptance_criteria.given: all required documents are provided
acceptance_criteria.then: all items are marked as provided and submission is enabled

stories.priority_rationale: Daniel calls this the biggest win, because six out of ten applications are incomplete today.
source_quotes: For me the biggest win would be if the system told the architect what is missing before they submit.
I'd say six out of ten applications are missing something.
The application form, site plan, floor plans, sections and elevations, the neighbour consent if it's close to the property line, and for larger projects an energy certificate.
stories.notes: Conditional documents are split out into US-4 (neighbour consent) and US-5 (energy certificate). Daniel also named missing signatures and the wrong plan scale; how these are checked online is an open question.

stories.title: Require neighbour consent near property line
stories.i_want: the system to block submission without a neighbour consent when the project is close to the property line
stories.so_that: I no longer have to chase missing neighbour consents by letter
stories.statement: As a permit clerk, I want the system to block submission without a neighbour consent when the project is close to the property line, so that I no longer have to chase missing neighbour consents by letter.

acceptance_criteria.given: the applicant has indicated that the project is close to the property line
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to submit without a neighbour consent document
acceptance_criteria.then: submission is blocked and the message names the neighbour consent as missing

acceptance_criteria.given: the applicant has indicated that the project is not close to the property line
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit without a neighbour consent
acceptance_criteria.then: submission is not blocked because of the neighbour consent

acceptance_criteria.given: the project is close to the property line and a neighbour consent is attached
acceptance_criteria.then: the submission succeeds

stories.priority_rationale: Daniel says this rule alone would save him hours every week.
source_quotes: If the form simply doesn't let them submit without the neighbour consent, I save hours every week.
the neighbour consent if it's close to the property line
stories.notes: The rule defining 'close to the property line' must be clarified (see open questions).

stories.title: Require energy certificate for larger projects
stories.i_want: the system to require an energy certificate for larger projects before submission
stories.so_that: larger projects are not submitted without it
stories.statement: As a permit clerk, I want the system to require an energy certificate for larger projects before submission, so that larger projects are not submitted without it.

acceptance_criteria.given: the project meets the defined criteria for a larger project
acceptance_criteria.when: the applicant tries to submit without an energy certificate
acceptance_criteria.then: submission is blocked and the energy certificate is listed as missing

acceptance_criteria.given: the project does not meet the criteria for a larger project
acceptance_criteria.when: the applicant submits without an energy certificate
acceptance_criteria.then: submission is not blocked because of the energy certificate

stories.priority_rationale: Daniel names it as a required document, but the threshold for a larger project is not yet defined.
source_quotes: and for larger projects an energy certificate
stories.notes: Blocked until the criteria for a 'larger project' are defined.

stories.title: Mark application as complete or incomplete
stories.i_want: to review a submitted dossier online and record whether it is complete
stories.so_that: I can do the completeness check without handling paper copies
stories.statement: As a permit clerk, I want to review a submitted dossier online and record whether it is complete, so that I can do the completeness check without handling paper copies.

acceptance_criteria.given: an application has the status "received"
acceptance_criteria.then: the clerk sees all form data and can open every uploaded document

acceptance_criteria.given: the clerk has checked the dossier
acceptance_criteria.then: the status changes to "in review" and the change is logged with the clerk's name and a timestamp

stories.priority_rationale: The completeness check is where most of the clerk's time goes, and online submission is useless without an online way to process it.
source_quotes: Daniel checks it for completeness
And the completeness check is where most of my time goes.

stories.title: Request additional documents online
stories.i_want: to request specific missing documents from the applicant through the portal
stories.so_that: I do not have to write a paper letter and wait for postal replies
stories.statement: As a permit clerk, I want to request specific missing documents from the applicant through the portal, so that I do not have to write a paper letter and wait for postal replies.

acceptance_criteria.given: the clerk finds that a document is missing
acceptance_criteria.when: they send a request naming the missing documents
acceptance_criteria.then: the application status changes to "additional documents needed" and the applicant sees the list of requested documents

acceptance_criteria.given: the status is "additional documents needed"
acceptance_criteria.when: the applicant uploads the requested documents and resubmits
acceptance_criteria.then: the clerk sees the newly uploaded documents in the dossier

stories.priority_rationale: It directly addresses the two-week letter cycle, but stakeholders only explicitly required submission and status tracking for the first version.
source_quotes: Then I write a letter, we wait two weeks, and the clock starts again.
If I could cut the completeness letters in half, I'd be happy.
stories.notes: Whether an online request is legally equivalent to a letter, including its deadline effects, must be clarified.

stories.title: View application status online
stories.i_want: to see the current status of my application online
stories.so_that: I do not have to call the building department to ask
stories.statement: As an applicant, I want to see the current status of my application online, so that I do not have to call the building department to ask.

acceptance_criteria.given: an applicant has submitted an application
acceptance_criteria.when: they open their application in the portal
acceptance_criteria.then: they see exactly one of the statuses "received", "in review", "additional documents needed" or "decision made"

acceptance_criteria.given: a clerk changes the status of an application
acceptance_criteria.when: the applicant next opens their application
acceptance_criteria.then: the new status and the date of the change are shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a user is not the applicant or an authorised representative of an application
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to open that application
acceptance_criteria.then: access is denied

stories.priority_rationale: Status tracking is explicitly required in the first version, and it addresses about ten status calls a day.
source_quotes: I get maybe ten calls a day just asking "what's the status?"
If they could see the status online, that would help a lot.
A status like "received", "in review", "additional documents needed", "decision made".
stories.notes: Status changes are made in US-6, US-7 and US-14. Notifications on status change were not discussed (see assumptions).

stories.title: Keep internal comments hidden from applicants
stories.i_want: internal comments and office statements to be hidden from applicants
stories.so_that: concerns, for example from fire protection, can be discussed internally before the applicant is informed
stories.statement: As the Head of Building Department, I want internal comments and office statements to be hidden from applicants, so that concerns, for example from fire protection, can be discussed internally before the applicant is informed.

acceptance_criteria.given: a reviewer or clerk has added an internal comment to a dossier
acceptance_criteria.then: the comment is not visible to the applicant

acceptance_criteria.given: an internal comment exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the applicant requests the application data through any portal page or download
acceptance_criteria.then: the internal comment is not included

stories.priority_rationale: Monika made this a condition of showing status online.
source_quotes: If the fire protection office has concerns, we don't want the applicant to see internal comments before we've discussed them.
So applicants should see the status, but not internal comments.

stories.title: Assign dossier to another office for review
stories.i_want: to assign a dossier to fire protection, environment or another office for review in the system
stories.so_that: I no longer copy plans and send them by internal mail
stories.statement: As a permit clerk, I want to assign a dossier to fire protection, environment or another office for review in the system, so that I no longer copy plans and send them by internal mail.

acceptance_criteria.given: a dossier is complete
acceptance_criteria.when: the clerk assigns it to the fire protection office
acceptance_criteria.then: the fire protection reviewers can see the dossier in their review list

acceptance_criteria.given: a dossier has been assigned to one office
acceptance_criteria.when: a reviewer from a different, unassigned office logs in
acceptance_criteria.then: that reviewer cannot see the dossier

stories.priority_rationale: Stakeholders described this as valuable, but it was not listed among the first-version must-haves.
source_quotes: We copy the plans and send them by internal mail.
then it goes around to the different offices: fire protection, environment, sometimes the canton.
stories.notes: Depends on US-12 (external access with roles). Cantonal routing is out of scope for now.

stories.title: Review plans and submit statement in the system
stories.i_want: to review the plans and submit my statement directly in the system
stories.so_that: I do not need paper copies and my statement reaches the building department without internal mail
stories.statement: As a fire protection reviewer, I want to review the plans and submit my statement directly in the system, so that I do not need paper copies and my statement reaches the building department without internal mail.

acceptance_criteria.given: a dossier has been assigned to the fire protection office
acceptance_criteria.then: they can view and download all plan documents

acceptance_criteria.given: the reviewer has written a statement
acceptance_criteria.then: the statement is attached to the dossier, marked as internal, and visible to the permit clerk

acceptance_criteria.given: a statement has been submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: the statement is not visible to the applicant

stories.priority_rationale: Daniel would welcome it given the average three-week review time, but it is not part of the first-version scope Monika defined.
source_quotes: It would be great if they could review directly in the system and leave their statement there.
Fire protection takes on average three weeks.
stories.notes: Depends on US-10, US-12 and US-9.

stories.title: External reviewer login with role
stories.i_want: to give reviewers from external authorities a personal login with a role limited to assigned dossiers
stories.so_that: the regional fire protection office can work in the system without access to unrelated data
stories.statement: As the IT coordinator, I want to give reviewers from external authorities a personal login with a role limited to assigned dossiers, so that the regional fire protection office can work in the system without access to unrelated data.

acceptance_criteria.given: the IT coordinator creates an account for an external reviewer with the role "fire protection reviewer"
acceptance_criteria.then: they see only the dossiers assigned to their office

acceptance_criteria.given: an external reviewer account has been deactivated
acceptance_criteria.when: the reviewer tries to log in
acceptance_criteria.then: login is refused

acceptance_criteria.given: an external reviewer is logged in
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to change an application's status
acceptance_criteria.then: the action is not permitted

stories.priority_rationale: It is required for external reviews, which stakeholders placed after online submission and status tracking.
source_quotes: The fire protection office is part of the regional authority, not the municipality, so they'd need external access.
That means we need proper login and roles.
stories.notes: Prerequisite for US-11. The authentication method is an open question.

stories.title: Show dossier access history for appeals
stories.i_want: to view and export the complete access and change history of a dossier
stories.so_that: in an appeal we can prove who saw and changed what
stories.statement: As the Head of Building Department, I want to view and export the complete access and change history of a dossier, so that in an appeal we can prove who saw and changed what.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user has opened a dossier
acceptance_criteria.when: the access history of that dossier is viewed
acceptance_criteria.then: an entry shows the user, the date and time, and the action "viewed"

acceptance_criteria.given: a user has changed data or a document in a dossier
acceptance_criteria.then: an entry shows the user, the date and time, and what was changed

acceptance_criteria.given: an authorised user requests an export of the history
acceptance_criteria.then: a file containing all entries of that dossier is produced

acceptance_criteria.given: any user, including administrators
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to edit or delete a history entry
acceptance_criteria.then: the action is not possible

stories.priority_rationale: Sandra states this is legally necessary because building permits are legal proceedings.
source_quotes: And every access to a dossier should be logged, because these are legal proceedings.
If there's an appeal, we must be able to show who saw and changed what.
stories.notes: Implements NFR-2. The roles allowed to view and export the history need to be confirmed.

stories.title: Consent to electronic delivery
stories.i_want: to give or withhold my consent to electronic delivery of the decision
stories.so_that: I receive the ruling through the channel I agreed to
stories.statement: As an applicant, I want to give or withhold my consent to electronic delivery of the decision, so that I receive the ruling through the channel I agreed to.

acceptance_criteria.given: an applicant is submitting an application
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose between electronic delivery and registered mail, with no option preselected

acceptance_criteria.given: an applicant has given consent
acceptance_criteria.then: the consent, the date and time and the applicant's identity are recorded in the dossier

acceptance_criteria.given: an applicant has not given consent
acceptance_criteria.then: the dossier shows that the decision must be sent by registered mail

stories.priority_rationale: Monika called consent legally important, but electronic delivery was not listed for the first version.
source_quotes: In the future it should be possible to deliver it electronically, but only if the applicant agrees to electronic delivery.
Legally that's important.
stories.notes: Prerequisite for US-15. Whether consent can be withdrawn later needs to be clarified.

stories.title: Deliver ruling electronically
stories.i_want: to deliver the signed ruling electronically to applicants who have consented
stories.so_that: we no longer need registered mail for these applicants
stories.statement: As a permit clerk, I want to deliver the signed ruling electronically to applicants who have consented, so that we no longer need registered mail for these applicants.

acceptance_criteria.given: the applicant has consented to electronic delivery and the ruling is signed
acceptance_criteria.then: the applicant can download the ruling in the portal and the status changes to "decision made"

acceptance_criteria.given: the applicant has not consented
acceptance_criteria.when: the clerk tries to deliver electronically
acceptance_criteria.then: electronic delivery is blocked

acceptance_criteria.given: a ruling has been delivered electronically
acceptance_criteria.then: the date and time of delivery are recorded in the dossier

stories.priority_rationale: It is described as a future capability rather than part of the first version.
source_quotes: The decision is a formal ruling, signed by the council.
Today it's sent by registered mail.
stories.notes: Depends on US-14. The legal requirements for an electronic signature and proof of delivery must be clarified.

stories.title: Use the portal in German or English
stories.i_want: to switch the portal between German and English
stories.so_that: international residents can apply without language barriers
stories.statement: As an applicant, I want to switch the portal between German and English, so that international residents can apply without language barriers.

acceptance_criteria.given: an applicant is on any portal page
acceptance_criteria.then: all labels, instructions, validation messages and status names are shown in English

acceptance_criteria.given: an applicant has selected a language
acceptance_criteria.then: the selected language is kept

stories.priority_rationale: The council explicitly wants the portal in German and English, and both languages are cheaper to build in from the start.
source_quotes: The council wants the portal in German and English.
Seeberg is German-speaking, but we have many international residents who work for companies in the St. Gallen region.
stories.notes: Whether formal documents such as rulings must also be available in English is an open question.

stories.title: Digitise paper applications at the counter
stories.i_want: to scan a paper application and record it in the system on behalf of the applicant
stories.so_that: applicants who cannot use the portal are served while the internal process stays digital
stories.statement: As counter staff, I want to scan a paper application and record it in the system on behalf of the applicant, so that applicants who cannot use the portal are served while the internal process stays digital.

acceptance_criteria.given: an applicant hands in a paper application at the counter
acceptance_criteria.when: the counter staff enter the form data and upload the scanned documents
acceptance_criteria.then: an application is created with the status "received" and is marked as received on paper

acceptance_criteria.given: a paper application has been digitised
acceptance_criteria.then: it follows the same workflow as an online application

stories.priority_rationale: Stakeholders disagree on whether paper remains accepted, and Monika must decide this with the council.
source_quotes: That's why I think we should still accept paper.
Maybe the counter staff scan it in for him, but the process behind it should be digital only.
If we keep both channels forever, we never get rid of the double work.
stories.notes: Blocked by the council decision on the paper channel. Re-prioritise once that decision is made.

stories.title: Track share of online applications
stories.i_want: to see how many applications were submitted online versus on paper per month
stories.so_that: I can show the council the progress on digitalisation
stories.statement: As the Head of Building Department, I want to see how many applications were submitted online versus on paper per month, so that I can show the council the progress on digitalisation.

acceptance_criteria.given: applications have been received through both channels
acceptance_criteria.when: the Head of Building Department opens the report for a month
acceptance_criteria.then: the number of online and paper applications for that month is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: applications received additional-documents requests
acceptance_criteria.then: the number of applications that received at least one request is shown per month

stories.priority_rationale: It supports the success measures stakeholders named, but nobody requested a report directly.
source_quotes: Most applications come in online, Daniel spends less time chasing missing documents, and we get fewer phone calls.
The council wants to show progress on digitalisation this year
stories.notes: Depends on US-7 and US-17 for its data. Measuring phone calls is outside the system.

stories.title: Integration with the canton
stories.i_want: to send dossiers that require cantonal involvement to the canton electronically
stories.so_that: cantonal reviews no longer need paper
stories.statement: As a permit clerk, I want to send dossiers that require cantonal involvement to the canton electronically, so that cantonal reviews no longer need paper.

acceptance_criteria.given: a dossier requires cantonal involvement
acceptance_criteria.then: the dossier is transmitted to the canton and the transmission is recorded in the dossier history

stories.priority_rationale: Monika explicitly deferred cantonal integration to after the first version.
source_quotes: The integration with the canton can come later.
stories.notes: Placeholder for a later release. The interface with the canton is unknown.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All application data and documents shall be stored and processed exclusively in data centres located in Switzerland.
source_quotes: Data has to stay in Switzerland, that's a clear requirement from the canton's data protection office.
we can't just put everything into some cloud in America

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Every access to a dossier (view, download, change) shall be logged with user, timestamp and action. Log entries shall be tamper-proof and retained at least as long as the dossier.
source_quotes: And every access to a dossier should be logged, because these are legal proceedings.
If there's an appeal, we must be able to show who saw and changed what.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The public portal shall meet the federal accessibility standard applicable to public websites and shall be fully operable with screen readers. The exact standard and conformance level are to be confirmed.
source_quotes: Public websites have to meet the federal accessibility standard.
We had complaints last year about our website not working with screen readers.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The full user interface shall be available in German and English.
source_quotes: The council wants the portal in German and English.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Building files shall be retained for the lifetime of the building. Other documents such as correspondence shall follow a retention period still to be confirmed with the archive (currently assumed to be ten years).
source_quotes: Building files are kept for the life of the building, basically forever.
Other documents like correspondence, I think ten years, but I'd need to check with the archive.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The system shall accept PDF uploads of at least 200 MB per file. A measurable upload time target is to be defined.
source_quotes: Some files are huge, 200 megabytes is not unusual.
And please, it has to be fast.
If uploading plans takes forever, architects will just keep sending paper.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Access shall require authenticated personal logins with role-based permissions, including roles for external authorities restricted to the dossiers assigned to them.
source_quotes: That means we need proper login and roles.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Rulings shall be delivered electronically only to applicants who have recorded consent to electronic delivery. All other applicants shall receive the ruling by registered mail.
source_quotes: but only if the applicant agrees to electronic delivery
Legally that's important.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The applicant submission flow shall be usability-tested with private homeowners, including older people with limited computer experience, before go-live. Pass criteria are to be agreed with the Product Owner.
source_quotes: They're often older and not very comfortable with computers.
But we also have private homeowners who want to build a garden shed or install solar panels.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The first version covering online submission and status tracking shall go live by next summer.
source_quotes: The council wants a first version live by next summer.
but submission online and status tracking should be there.

open_questions.question: Will paper applications still be accepted, and if so, who digitises them? Daniel Rossi wants to keep accepting paper, while Monika Keller wants a digital-only process, possibly with counter staff scanning applications.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is a contradiction between stakeholders. It determines whether US-17 is needed and whether a dual process must be supported.
open_questions.ask_whom: Monika Keller together with the council

open_questions.question: How will missing signatures be handled online? Is a signature still required, and if so, which form of electronic signature or identification replaces it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Daniel named missing signatures as a common reason for incompleteness, and the legal validity of an online submission depends on the answer.
open_questions.ask_whom: Monika Keller and the legal service

open_questions.question: How is 'close to the property line' defined (distance threshold), and how does the system know it? Is it applicant self-declaration or based on plan data?
open_questions.why_it_matters: US-4 cannot be implemented or tested without a clear rule.

open_questions.question: What defines a 'larger project' that requires an energy certificate?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The conditional check in US-5 needs a clear criterion.

open_questions.question: Can the system check the plan scale automatically, or does this remain a manual check?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Daniel named a wrong plan scale as a frequent defect, and automatic checking could reduce completeness letters further.

open_questions.question: What is the maximum file size per document and per application, and what upload time is acceptable for a 200 MB file on a typical connection?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 'Fast' is not testable. A measurable target is needed for NFR-6 and US-2.
open_questions.ask_whom: Daniel Rossi and Sandra Frei, ideally validated with a few architects

open_questions.question: Which federal accessibility standard and conformance level must be met?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The acceptance tests for NFR-3 depend on the exact standard.

open_questions.question: What is the retention period for correspondence and other non-building-file documents?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Sandra was unsure about ten years, and deletion rules must be implemented correctly.
open_questions.ask_whom: Sandra Frei together with the municipal archive

open_questions.question: How will applicants and external reviewers authenticate (for example with a cantonal or national electronic identity, or local accounts)? Can an architect act on behalf of an owner?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This affects US-1, US-8 and US-12, as well as the representation rights of architects.

open_questions.question: What are the legal requirements for electronic delivery: the form of the council's electronic signature, proof of delivery, and whether consent can be withdrawn?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Monika stressed that this is legally important, and the design of US-14 and US-15 depends on it.
open_questions.ask_whom: Monika Keller and the legal service

open_questions.question: When and how may internal comments or office statements be shared with the applicant, and who decides?
open_questions.why_it_matters: US-9 only defines hiding comments. A controlled release process may be needed.

open_questions.question: Do the environment office and the canton need the same review access as fire protection in the first version or later?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This defines the scope of E4 and the role model.

open_questions.question: Should applicants be notified (for example by email) when the status changes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without notifications, applicants may still call. This was not discussed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact go-live date for 'next summer', and which stories form the minimum first version?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is needed for release planning and to confirm the Must priorities.

open_questions.question: Must rulings and other formal documents also be available in English, or only the portal interface?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Translating legal documents has a much larger impact than translating the user interface.

assumptions: Architects and builders submit on behalf of owners, so the portal must support representation of an owner by an architect.
The four statuses named by Monika are sufficient for the first version.
Status changes are made manually by permit clerks.
Internal comments and office statements are visible only to municipal staff and assigned reviewers.
The new solution needs its own storage infrastructure, because the current file server cannot handle large files.
Baseline figures for measuring success are six out of ten applications incomplete and about ten status calls a day.
out_of_scope: Integration with the canton in the first version (explicitly deferred).
Showing internal comments or office statements to applicants.
Electronic delivery of rulings to applicants who have not consented.
